findings.title: Child timeout equals context deadline and may be non-positive
findings.message: The child's -test.timeout is set to exactly the time left before ctx expires. The context kills the child at about the same moment the child's timeout fires, so the child is often killed before it can print its panic and goroutine dump. That loses the diagnostic the timeout exists to provide. The value is also computed after the build has used up part of the budget. It can be zero or negative, and testing treats a timeout <= 0 as no timeout, so the guard silently disappears.
findings.suggestion: Compute the remaining time after the build. Fail if too little remains. Give the child a timeout slightly shorter than ctx so it reports a timeout before ctx kills it.

findings.title: No WaitDelay: CombinedOutput may hang after context kill
findings.message: When ctx expires, CommandContext kills only the `go` process. Subprocesses it started, such as compile and link, can keep the stdout/stderr pipe open. CombinedOutput then blocks until they exit, which can go past the outer test deadline. This defeats the new goal of leaving the parent time to report.
findings.suggestion: Set build.WaitDelay (and command.WaitDelay) to a short duration so Wait returns soon after cancellation even if pipes stay open.
